Rule.Title: Reputation (Homebrew)
Rule.Intro: Each character has a reputation with every faction they have encountered. It uses the same scale as the relationships between factions, from Nemeses (−3) to Close Allies (+3), and every character starts at Neutral.
Rule.Marks: When a character does something the faction would hear about, the GM marks reputation: a positive mark for deeds that help the faction or its people, a negative mark for deeds that harm or shame it. Every {per} marks in one direction shift the rating one step. Marks in the other direction erase marks first, so a reputation can climb back from the brink.
Rule.MarksOne: When a character does something the faction would hear about, the GM shifts their rating one step up for deeds that help the faction or its people, or one step down for deeds that harm or shame it.
Rule.Shifts: Big deeds (saving a leader, exposing a spy, burning a temple) can be worth several marks at once. The faction's allies and enemies may react too: consider a mark with factions that are Allies or Nemeses of the one affected.

Effect.Title: At the table
Effect.closeAllies: The faction takes real risks for you. Once per session, call on it for significant aid. Advantage on rolls to influence its members.
Effect.allies: Members help even at some cost to themselves. Advantage on rolls to influence its members.
Effect.friendly: Members render help that doesn't need much effort or risk.
Effect.unfriendly: Members are unhelpful; even small favors come at a price.
Effect.enemies: Members hinder you. Disadvantage on rolls to influence them.
Effect.nemeses: The faction goes out on a limb to see you suffer. Disadvantage on rolls to influence its members, and the GM may make a move against you when you're recognized.

Objectives.Title: Objective Countdowns
Objectives.Hint: Plan each objective here, then start it as a countdown in the Countdowns tracker and tick it there. Advance one countdown per faction each in-game week. Major objectives take 10 steps, minor ones 4 to 6. A faction can pursue one major and up to two minor objectives at a time.
Objectives.StartHint: Add this objective to the Countdowns tracker as a narrative countdown
Objectives.Started: {name} is now in the Countdowns tracker.
Objectives.Done: Countdown complete: the objective is achieved. Pick a new objective based on the fiction.
Objectives.RemoveConfirm: Remove {name}? Its countdown is removed from the Countdowns tracker too.

Notify.RingMissing: Five Banners: the installed Daggerheart Core Rulebook module has no Five Banners Burning token ring art. Update that module, or turn off the token ring option.

SheetTheme.Name: Five Banners Burning sheet theme
SheetTheme.Hint: Show every sheet that supports the Core Rulebook themes in the Five Banners Burning theme, whatever theme each user picked. Turning this off (or disabling the module) brings back everyone's own choice.

TokenRing.Name: Five Banners Burning token ring
TokenRing.Hint: Use the Core Rulebook module's Five Banners Burning dynamic token ring instead of the ring picked in Foundry's settings.

Reputation.Name: Reputation (homebrew)
Reputation.Hint: Track each character's reputation with the factions they've met, on the Factions tab.

MarksPerRank.Name: Reputation marks per step
MarksPerRank.Hint: How many marks shift a reputation one step on the Nemeses to Close Allies scale. Set to 1 to move the rating directly.

PlayersMark.Name: Players can mark reputation
PlayersMark.Hint: Let players change the reputation of characters they own. Otherwise only the GM can.

Mirror.Name: Mirror faction relationships
Mirror.Hint: When you set how one faction feels about another, set the same rating the other way around.
